newsitem.title: GERMANY: Uncertainty over U.S. soy buoys N.Europe rapeseed.
newsitem.headline: Uncertainty over U.S. soy buoys N.Europe rapeseed.

text.p: North European rapeseed prices were steady as the soy market faced possible disruption because of opposition to genetically altered U.S. beans, brokers said.
"Trades are extremely slim because consumers think prices are too high...they would rather reduce crushings than operate unprofitably," one said on Friday.
"But the soya row is beginning to creep in because it strengthens rape oil versus soyoil in northern Europe."
Environmentalist group Greenpeace plans to organise protests against genetically manipulated U.S. soybeans, which are officially approved for import into the EU in late 1996.
Earlier on Friday Greenpeace issued a list of German firms opposed to the use of genetically manipulated soy in food products or in favour of special labelling.
Rape oil cif Rotterdam was today quoted at $101 a tonne for Nov/Jan, at a premium to soyoil at $96.
Prices were also supported by reports that German winter rape sowings might be reduced by 15-20 percent due to lower set-aside.
Another supportive factor was talk of low oil content -- 40 percent is the tradeable norm -- in the northern German 1996 rapeseed harvest.
Buyers free Hamburg kept September seed steady on the week at 470 marks but offered 2.50 more for October.
Buyers at other points left the September range broadly unchanged at 455-467.
October rapeseed was nominally pegged at 475 ciffo in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp range and at 465-467.50 fob Baltic ports after Polish buyers paid 463 fob Baltic.
The November position on the Paris Matif futures exchange was last in an untraded 471-475 marks range.
Local rape meal sellers kept Sept/October (34 percent protein) steady at 28.75-29.00 marks/100kg, while Nov/Jan was up 0.25 at 28.75.
By comparison, spot soymeal cost 46.00 marks (44 percent protein).
Oct rape oil was at 86.75 marks/100 kg, down 2.25 on the week, with Nov-Jan at 89.50, down 1.50.
